pg006_n0008: This textbook, Mathematics for Secondary Schools, is written specifically for Form One students in the United Republic of Tanzania.
pg006_n0009: The book is prepared in accordance with the twenty twenty-three Mathematics Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education, Form One through Form Four, issued by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology.
pg006_n0010: It is a revised edition of Basic Mathematics for Secondary Schools Student’s Book for Form One that was published in twenty nineteen in accordance with the two thousand five syllabus issued by the then Ministry of Education and Vocational Training, M O E V T.
pg006_n0012: The book consists of six chapters, namely: Concept of Mathematics, Numbers, Approximations, Ratios and proportions, Algebra, and Coordinate geometry.
pg006_n0013: In addition to the contents, each chapter contains activities, illustrations, projects, and exercises.
pg006_n0014: You are encouraged to do all the activities, projects and attempt all questions in the exercises.
pg006_n0015: This will enhance your understanding and development of the intended competencies for this level.

pg007_im006: Introduction text box explaining that mathematics is all around us, used in many fields and technologies, and that the chapter covers the meaning, branches, relationships, and importance of mathematics in solving everyday problems.
pg007_n0012: Almost everything we do involves Mathematics.
pg007_n0013: It is applied in various fields such as science, engineering, technology, social studies, economics and many others.
pg007_n0014: Numerous devices such as mobile phones, computers, television sets, and satellites are designed and manufactured on the basis of mathematical knowledge.
pg007_n0015: In this chapter, you will learn about the meaning of Mathematics, branches of Mathematics, relationship between Mathematics and other subjects, and the importance of studying Mathematics.
pg007_n0016: The competencies developed will enable you to apply Mathematics knowledge and skills to solve daily life problems in different fields such as Agriculture, Entrepreneurship, Botany, Zoology, Music, History, Business, and many other fields.
pg007_n0020: The word Mathematics comes from the Greek word mathema, meaning which is learnt or science, knowledge or learning.
pg007_n0021: Numbers, measurements, shapes of physical objects, and equations form a small part of it.
pg007_n0022: Mathematics can be thought of as the science of the structures, orders, patterns, and relations that have evolved from elementary practices of counting, measuring, and describing the shapes of objects.
pg007_n0023: It can also be thought of as a language of science because by using mathematical reasoning, one can develop an understanding and be able to predict nature.
pg007_n0024: Mathematics has the ability to provide precise expression for every concept that can be formulated using mathematical symbols and structures.
pg007_n0025: The knowledge and skills of Mathematics play a crucial role in understanding the concepts of other subjects, both in sciences and arts.
pg007_n0029: Mathematics can be categorized into different branches such as Arithmetic, Algebra, and Geometry.
pg008_n0006: Arithmetic is a branch of Mathematics that deals with properties and manipulations of numbers.
pg008_n0007: Manipulation of numbers is achieved through the use of basic mathematical operations namely: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
pg008_n0011: Algebra is a branch of Mathematics in which arithmetic operations are applied to symbols rather than specific numbers.
pg008_n0012: The symbols or letters in algebra are called variables which represent quantities with no fixed values.
pg008_n0016: The word geometry was derived from the Greek word ‘Geo’, which means ‘earth’ and ‘metry’, which means ‘measurement’.
pg008_n0017: Therefore, Geometry is a branch of Mathematics which deals with the study of the sizes, shapes, positions, angles, and dimensions of different physical objects.
pg008_n0018: Moreover, properties of points, lines, planes, similarities, congruence, and shapes of different regular objects are also studied in Geometry.
pg008_n0020: Relationship between Mathematics and other subjects
pg008_n0022: Every aspect of our life makes use of Mathematics in one way or another.
pg008_n0023: Mathematics plays a major role as a tool for effective understanding of other subjects.
pg008_n0024: Numerous concepts in other subjects and fields are described precisely using Mathematics.
pg008_n0025: Learning Mathematics can also benefit students through developing their problem solving and critical thinking skills.
pg008_n0026: Note that, Mathematics formulas which are used to represent and describe concepts and scenarios in other fields are commonly referred to as mathematical models.
pg008_im003: Activity one point one, “Discovering the use of Mathematics in daily lives,” with three tasks: recall daily activities and identify applications of mathematics; represent the activities and mathematical skills using a table or another method; and explain the mathematical aspects observed.
pg008_n0029: Activity one point one: Discovering the use of Mathematics in daily lives
pg008_n0032: One. Recall your daily activities, identify and record applications of Mathematics in such activities.
pg008_n0034: Two. Use a table or any method of your choice to represent the identified activities and its mathematical skills obtained in step one.
pg008_n0036: Three. Explain the mathematical aspects you have observed in step two.
pg008_n0040: Agriculture is closely related to Mathematics.
pg008_n0041: For instance, when farmers want to buy seeds, they need to understand the ratio of seeds that is sufficient per piece of land.
pg009_n0004: Similarly, the determination of the number of bags of fertilizers needed per acre requires some calculations.
pg009_n0005: In these two examples, Mathematics enables farmers to avoid the wastage of financial resources by purchasing only the required amount of inputs.
pg009_n0006: Mathematics is also used in Agriculture to determine suitable amount of water to be used in irrigation and the spacing between seedlings.
pg009_n0007: Similarly, Mathematics is used to determine the investment, expenditure, and savings in cultivating a specific crop, dividing a piece of land, calculating the cost of labour, and so forth.
pg009_n0011: There is a direct relationship between Mathematics and Biology.
pg009_n0012: For example, normal animal weights, rate of respiration, nutritive values of food, and transpiration are a few quantities in Biology that can be calculated using mathematical concepts.
pg009_n0013: Mathematics can also be used to estimate the number of blood cells present in the body, measurement of blood pressure, and counting sex chromosomes, among many others.
pg009_n0017: Mathematics is widely applied in Chemistry to represent and solve various problems.
pg009_n0018: Some Chemistry activities involve measurement of masses, volumes, lengths, temperatures and densities of matter.
pg009_n0019: Mathematics is also used to measure the constituents of mixtures, balancing chemical equations, among many other applications.
pg009_n0023: Physics involves the study of laws, principles, and theorems which governs how matter works.
pg009_n0024: Most of the quantities in Physics are expressed mathematically through formulas.
pg009_n0025: In order to understand how to apply the formulas to solve some physics challenges, knowledge of Mathematics is needed.
pg009_n0026: All the quantities in physics are expressed in numbers and units which have to be manipulated using the concepts and skills of Mathematics.
pg009_n0027: For example, to determine the speed of a moving object, one has to find a ratio between the distance covered and the time taken.
pg009_n0029: Mathematics and Information and Communications Technology
pg009_n0031: Mathematics plays a big role in the field of Information and Communications Technology, open parenthesis I C T close parenthesis.
pg009_n0032: Computer programs, applications, software, and computer languages make use of mathematical concepts.
pg009_n0033: A common example of the application of numbers is in defining colours in web development languages.
pg009_n0034: For instance, the HTML, open parenthesis hypertext markup language close parenthesis, and CSS, open parenthesis cascading style sheets close parenthesis, uses colour notations such as number sign zero zero zero zero zero zero which represent Black, number sign zero zero eight zero zero zero for Green and number sign eight zero zero zero zero zero for Maroon.
pg009_n0035: Furthermore, the digits zero and one are commonly used in computing systems in computers.
pg010_n0005: Mathematics is widely applied in daily life activities related to Business Studies.
pg010_n0006: For example, if one wants to determine profit or loss in business, a difference between the selling and buying prices is to be calculated.
pg010_n0007: If the buying price is less than the selling price, the business makes profit.
pg010_n0008: If the buying price is higher than the selling price, the business makes loss.
pg010_n0009: Mathematics is also applied in other areas such as in loan borrowing, determining prices of items, among many other applications.
pg010_n0012: Geographers require mathematical calculations to find the distance from one place to another, finding gradients, altitudes of hills and mountains.
pg010_n0013: Through mathematical calculations, geographical locations of different places are determined using latitudes and longitudes, and real-life objects such as buildings are represented on a map through the use of scales.
pg010_n0016: Mathematics helps in describing various historical activities such as duration of events and expressing historical events which happened at different points in time.
pg010_n0017: For example, a simple mathematical operation is used to determine duration of historical events such as World Wars, colonial periods and time spent by leaders in positions, determining dates and ages of fossils by using some mathematical principles such as carbon fourteen among many other applications.
pg010_n0020: Mastering basic concepts of arithmetic can enable a person to understand better and manage literary works.
pg010_n0021: A kind of writing which can draw attention to readers depend on several factors such as number of words per sentence, the number of sentences per paragraph, and the number of paragraphs per page.
pg010_n0022: For example, twenty words in a sentence are considered as average.
pg010_n0023: Thus, in analysing writing style, one need to find an average number of words in each sentence, which requires Mathematics concepts.
pg010_n0026: The knowledge of Mathematics plays a vital role in music.
pg010_n0027: For instance, playing one note in piano has a different sound as when three harmonic notes are played together.
pg010_n0028: Music notes are distinguished mathematically by their different values.
pg011_n0003: A semibreve has four beats, a minim has two beats, crotchet has one beat, quaver has one half a bit, semi quaver has one quarter a bit, and so on.
pg011_n0004: Reading and playing music represented by notes in a music sheet depends on the mathematical ability to understand these values.
pg011_n0008: Mathematics is important in all forms of sports and games.
pg011_n0009: For example, in many sports and games, winners are those who have accumulated highest number of points.
pg011_n0010: Furthermore, in most of the sports and games, there are specific number of players in the playing ground.
pg011_n0011: For instance, a football team has eleven players while a netball team has seven players.
pg011_n0012: Moreover, players in some games such as football are given names in terms of numbers.
pg011_n0013: In football, a goalkeeper is normally assigned number one.
pg011_n0014: In addition, all playing grounds are prepared with specific standards of measurements.
pg011_n0016: Activity one point two: Exploring the use of Mathematics in other fields
pg011_n0017: Explore various resources such as books and internet to discover examples of mathematical concepts and skills that are used in three subjects other than those discussed in this chapter.
pg011_n0021: Learning Mathematics and using mathematical skills in daily life enhances problem solving, critical thinking, effective time management among many other importances.
pg011_n0025: Financial management requires mathematical skills during the preparation of budgets.
pg011_n0026: Calculations are done to ensure the budget prepared correlates with the funds collected.
pg011_n0030: Problem-solving is one of the most important skills in life.
pg011_n0031: Mathematics is one of the most effective ways to increase analytical and logical thinking, which helps us to become better problem solvers.
pg011_n0035: Time management is a key to success for everyone.
pg011_n0036: Therefore, time must be carefully managed.
pg011_n0037: Mathematics helps to determine the time spent on every activity so as to maximize its efficiency.

pg013_n0009: Numbers play a vital role in everyday life.
pg013_n0010: Different activities are performed with the help of numbers.
pg013_n0011: Numbers are used to quantify and measure quantities.
pg013_n0012: For instance, length, mass, time, volume, and population are some of the quantities represented by numbers.
pg013_n0013: In this chapter, you will learn about rational, irrational, and real numbers.
pg013_n0014: You will also learn about repeating decimals, inequalities, and absolute values of real numbers.
pg013_n0015: The competencies developed will enable you to perform daily life activities such as counting things, managing money, distributing items, and interpreting numbers based on contexts, and many other applications.
pg013_n0019: Numbers are classified into different categories.
pg013_n0020: Some categories of numbers that you have already learned include whole numbers, natural numbers, fractions, integers, and decimals.
pg013_n0021: Other major categories of numbers include rational, irrational, and real numbers.
pg013_n0022: Activity two point one enables you to identify categories of numbers from daily life activities.
pg013_n0025: Activity two point one: Categorising numbers

pg013_n0032: Record the measurements in task one and categorise them based on your understanding of categories of numbers.

pg014_n0004: Fractions, integers, whole numbers, terminating and non-terminating decimals form the set of rational numbers.
pg014_n0005: For instance, thirty-four over three, negative twenty over three, negative three, negative four over seven, negative five over six, one half, one third, four over four, nine over five, one hundred over five, zero, thirty over one, zero point four five, zero point three repeating, zero point two three repeating, and one point five six seven repeating are rational numbers.
pg014_n0007: Representation of rational numbers on a number line
pg014_n0009: Rational numbers can be represented on a number line.
pg014_n0010: Positive rational numbers are represented on the right of zero, the origin, and the negative rational numbers on the left of the origin.
pg014_n0011: The number line helps us to determine other rational numbers between any two rational numbers by increasing the number of divisions.

pg014_n0030: The representation of any positive rational number a over b is done by dividing the unit interval into b equal parts.
pg014_n0031: The a of these parts are taken along the number line to reach the point corresponding to a over b on the right of zero if the number is positive, and to the left of zero if the number is negative.

pg015_n0007: In order to represent one fourth on a number line, take one unit from zero towards the right side and then divide that unit into four equal parts.

pg017_n0069: Decimal numbers are part of rational numbers and are common in our daily life activities.
pg017_n0070: The quantities such as length, height, age, volume and mass can be presented in decimals.

pg018_n0020: A repeating decimal, also known as recurring decimal, is a decimal number with at least one digit in the decimal part that repeats consecutively in a regular order without an end.
pg018_n0021: For instance, one point six repeating and zero point six three nine repeating are repeating decimals because six and the digits six three nine from the two decimal numbers, respectively, in the decimal part repeat themselves without an end.
pg018_n0022: The three dots indicate that the repeating digits continue infinitely.
pg018_n0024: Repeating decimals can also be represented by using a dot or a bar that is placed on top of a repeating digit.
pg018_n0029: Write each of the following repeating decimals by using a dot and a bar.

pg018_n0036: zero point six three nine six three nine six three nine
pg018_n0039: zero point four seven four seven four seven four seven four
pg018_n0045: zero point three three three three is a repeating decimal which can be written as zero point three dot or zero point three repeating
pg018_n0048: zero point six three nine six three nine six three nine can be written as zero point six three nine, with a dot over the six and the nine, or zero point six three nine repeating
pg018_n0051: zero point four seven four seven four seven four seven four can be written as zero point four seven, with a dot over the four and the seven, or zero point four seven repeating
pg018_n0053: In Example two point four, the digits with a dot or a bar are repeating infinitely.
pg018_n0054: In b and c, it can be observed that if a group of digits is repeating, a dot should be put over the first and the last repeating digits.
pg018_n0056: Decimals are either terminating or non-terminating.
pg018_n0057: Terminating decimals have a definite number of digits after the decimal point while non-terminating decimals have an endless number of digits after the decimal point.
pg018_n0058: Thus, repeating decimals are non-terminating with one or more repeating digits in the decimal part.
pg019_n0004: Examples of terminating decimals are zero point five, one point four, and seven point nine, while non-terminating decimals are three point one four one five nine two six, one point four one four two one three five, and two point two three six zero six seven nine, and so on.
pg019_n0008: When working with problems involving repeating decimals, it is important to convert them into simple fractions to maintain accuracy and avoid errors.
pg019_n0009: A repeating decimal can be converted into fraction using the following steps:
pg019_n0012: one. Choose any variable to represent the required fraction.
pg019_n0014: two. Multiply both sides of the equation by a multiple of ten depending on the number of repeating decimals.
pg019_n0015: For instance, zero point eight repeating and zero point two one three repeating have only one repeating digit, which means they are multiplied by ten.
pg019_n0016: Decimal numbers zero point one one repeating and one point two one four repeating have two repeating digits, thus they are multiplied by one hundred, and zero point eight three five repeating will be multiplied by one thousand since it has three repeating digits.
pg019_n0018: three. Subtract the equation in step one from the equation in step two.
pg019_n0020: four. From the equation obtained in step three, solve for the chosen variable and simplify where necessary.

pg030_n0027: In Mathematics, an inequality is a statement that compares or relates two values or expressions.
pg030_n0028: The common terms involved in comparing the values or expressions are “less than”, “greater than”, “greater than or equal to”, “less than or equal to”, or “not equal to”.
pg030_n0029: For instance, the following statements are examples of inequalities:

pg031_n0005: In general, mathematical statements which use not equal to, greater than, less than, greater than or equal to, or less than or equal to are called inequalities.
pg031_n0010: The sharp end of greater than and less than always points to a smaller number.
pg031_n0012: The symbols less than or equal to and greater than or equal to are sometimes referred to as at most and at least, respectively.
pg031_n0014: If the inequality is divided or multiplied on both sides by a negative number, the direction of the inequality sign changes.

pg031_n0021: Generally, on a number line, a number to the right side of another number is always greater than a number to its left side.
pg031_n0022: Thus, from the number line, b is greater than a, which can also be written as b is greater than a.
pg031_n0023: c is greater than b, which can also be written as c is greater than b.
pg031_n0024: The vice versa is also true, that is, a number which is on the left side of another number on a number line is always less than the number on its right side.
pg031_n0025: That is, a is less than b and b is less than c.

pg039_n0004: Absolute value of a real number
pg039_n0006: The absolute value of a real number x, denoted by the absolute value of x, is the non-negative value of x regardless of its sign.
pg039_n0007: For instance, the absolute value of 2 equals 2, and the absolute value of negative 2 equals 2.
pg039_im004: Number line from negative 2 to 2 with 0 at the center; arrows above show that the distance from 0 to negative 2 and from 0 to 2 is 2 units in each direction.
pg039_n0010: The distance from 0 to negative 2 and that from 0 to 2 is the same, that is, 2 units.
pg039_n0011: Thus, 2 is an absolute value of both 2 and negative 2.
pg039_n0012: The absolute value of a number is the magnitude of that number regardless of its sign.
pg039_n0014: The absolute value of a number x is written as the absolute value of x, such that the absolute value of x equals x if x is greater than or equal to 0, and the absolute value of x equals negative x if x is less than 0, and its distance is represented on a number line from 0.
pg039_n0015: This distance is always positive or zero.
pg039_n0017: For instance: the absolute value of 0.75 equals 0.75, the absolute value of negative 0.143 equals 0.143, the absolute value of negative one half equals one half, the absolute value of 0 equals 0, and the absolute value of negative 2 equals 2.
pg039_n0019: In general, for any two positive and negative numbers x and negative x, their absolute values are equal, that is, the absolute value of x equals the absolute value of negative x.

pg046_n0010: Understanding approximations is important in our daily life.
pg046_n0011: Approximations are used in various real life situations like estimating cost of items, distances, and ingredients for a recipe.
pg046_n0012: In this chapter, you will learn about rounding off numbers by place values, number of decimal places and by significant figures.
pg046_n0013: Also, you will learn how to perform approximation in calculations.
pg046_n0014: The competencies developed will help you to perform real-life activities such as estimating number of things, analysing large data, making quick calculations, preparing budgets, and many other applications.
pg046_n0018: Approximation is a process of finding a number that is closest to the exact value.
pg046_n0019: It involves expressing a number into a higher or lower value which is close to the exact value.
pg046_n0020: Approximation can be termed as estimation and is represented by the symbol approximately equal to.

pg046_n0036: Rounding off numbers is a process of making a number simpler, but keeping its value closer to the original value.
pg046_n0037: The outcome is less precise but more user-friendly.
pg046_n0038: Rounding off the number can be done by considering place values, number of decimal places, and number of significant figures.
pg047_n0004: Rounding off numbers by place values
pg047_n0006: Rounding off numbers by place values is done by considering the given place value for both whole and decimal parts of a number.
pg047_n0007: Thus, for whole numbers, it can be done to the nearest ones, tens, hundreds, thousands or any other place value.
pg047_n0008: For decimal numbers, it can be done to the nearest tenths, hundredths, thousandths and so on.
pg047_n0009: The following are basic procedures for rounding off numbers by place values.
pg047_n0011: a, If the digit to the right of the rounding digit is either zero, one, two, three, or four, then the digit at the required place value remains unchanged, and each digit to the right of it become zeros.
pg047_n0015: A rounding digit is the digit at a place where a number is supposed to be rounded off.

pg047_n0031: In this case, maintain 6 and replace each digit to the right of 6 with zero.

pg051_n0037: Rounding off decimals involves a similar process of rounding numbers by place values.
pg051_n0038: When rounding off decimals, the digits to the right of the given decimal place are dropped rather than being replaced by zeros.
pg051_n0040: In the process of rounding off, the following steps are used:
pg051_n0041: open parenthesis a close parenthesis, If the digit after the rounding digit is either zero, one, two, three, or four, then the rounding digit remain unchanged, and all the other digits to the right are dropped.
pg051_n0046: Round off zero point two four six four to three decimal places.
pg051_n0050: The digit in the third decimal place is six and the nearest digit to the right is four which is less than five.

pg051_n0052: Therefore, zero point two four six four is approximately equal to zero point two four six to three decimal places.
pg052_n0003: open parenthesis b close parenthesis, If the digit to the right of a rounding digit is greater than five, then one is added to the rounding digit and other digits to the right are dropped.

pg055_n0041: A significant figure is a digit in a number that gives information about the precision and accuracy of the measured value.
pg055_n0046: 1. Any digit from 1 to 9 appearing in a number is a significant figure.
pg055_n0048: 2. Each zero appearing in a number between digits 1 to 9 is a significant figure.
pg055_n0049: For example, 0 in 602 is a significant figure.
pg055_n0052: 3. When zeros are written to the right of the last non-zero digit, the zeros are not significant figures.
pg055_n0053: For example, 72,000 has only 2 significant figures.
pg055_n0055: 4. In decimals, any zero to the left of the first non-zero digit is not a significant figure.
pg055_n0056: For example, the zeros in 0.025 are not significant figures.
pg055_n0059: 5. All zeros that are on the right of a decimal point are significant only if a non-zero digit does not follow them.
pg055_n0060: For example, 0.040 has two significant figures while 0.6700 has four significant figures, and 10.000 has five significant figures.
pg056_n0007: When zero is written at the end of an approximated number, including decimals, it is a significant figure.
pg056_n0008: For example, 2.73 is approximately equal to 3.0, and in this case, 0 is a significant figure.
pg056_n0009: Also, 45,961 is approximately equal to 46,000; the zero at the third-place value is a significant figure.
pg056_n0013: All the zeros that are on the right of the non-zero digit are significant if they come from measurements.
pg056_n0014: For instance, 20 meters has two significant figures and 300 grams has 3 significant figures.
pg056_n0019: open parenthesis i close parenthesis, Significant figures are also known as significant digits.
pg056_n0021: open parenthesis i i close parenthesis, Significant figures are always counted from left towards the right of a number.

pg056_n0065: The first digit, 3, is increased by one to become 4, since 8 is greater than 5, and each of the right-side digits become zero.
pg056_n0066: Thus, 38,176 is approximately equal to 40,000, correct to 1 significant figure.

pg061_n0078: One. Approximating or rounding off a number is a process of writing a number close enough to the exact number.

pg061_n0083: Roman numeral one: increased by one if it is odd.
pg061_n0085: item two, left unchanged if it is even and has zero digits after five or has no digit after five.
pg062_n0008: item three, any digit from one to nine appearing in a number is a significant figure.
pg062_n0009: item four, when zeros are written to the right of the last non-zero digit of an exact number, the zeros are not significant figures.
pg062_n0010: three. In decimals, any zero written to the left of the first non-zero digit is not a significant figure.
pg062_n0011: four. All zeros that are on the right of the decimal point are significant, only if a non-zero digit does not follow them.
pg062_n0012: five. When a zero is written at the end of an approximated decimal or number, it is a significant figure.
pg062_n0013: six. All the zeros that are on the right of the last non-zero digit are significant if they come from measurements.

pg067_im004: Chapter Four heading: Ratios and proportions.
pg067_im005: Introduction box explaining that ratios and proportions are important in everyday life, including cooking, finance, medicine, construction, arts and design, balancing diets, distributing items, and planning events, and that the chapter develops skills for equal and proportional sharing and distribution.
pg067_n0009: Ratios and proportions play an important role in our everyday life.
pg067_n0010: They are used in various daily life activities such as in cooking, financial activities, medicine prescription, construction, arts and design, and many more applications.
pg067_n0011: Understanding proportions helps us manage various daily life activities such as balancing diets, distributing things, and planning of events.
pg067_n0012: In this chapter, you will learn about ratios and proportions.
pg067_n0013: The competencies developed will enable you to ensure equal and proportional sharing and distribution of things among other applications.
pg067_n0017: Sharing things is a common practice in our life.
pg067_n0018: For example, people can share portions of land, wealth, and many other things.
pg067_n0019: A required portion of water, fruit paste and sugar can result into a nice juice.

pg067_n0036: A ratio is a quantitative comparison between two or more quantities of the same units, normally expressed as a fraction.
pg067_n0037: It shows the number of times one value contains the other.
pg067_n0038: A ratio between the numbers p and q is written as p to q, which is equivalent to p divided by q or p over q, and is read as p to q.
pg067_n0039: It should be noted that multiplying
pg068_n0007: or dividing both terms of a ratio by the same number does not change the ratio.
pg068_n0008: In other words, two to four equals four to eight, multiplying each term of the ratio by two.
pg068_n0009: The ratio can be reduced to its lowest terms by expressing the ratio as a fraction and simplify it to its lowest term.
pg068_n0018: The given ratio can be written in fraction as forty-eight over thirty-six.
pg068_n0019: Dividing the numerator and denominator by twelve gives,
pg068_n0020: Forty-eight over thirty-six equals four over three.
pg068_n0021: Therefore, forty-eight to thirty-six in its simplified form is four to three.
pg068_n0026: Given a to b equals one to two, and b to c equals three to five, find a to b to c and a to c.
pg068_n0029: Given a to b equals one to two, and b to c equals three to five.
pg068_n0030: b is in both ratios, so make the two ratios equivalent by multiplying a to b equals one to two by three and b to c equals three to five by two as follows:
pg068_n0031: a to b equals the quantity one to two, times three
pg068_n0032: b to c equals the quantity three to five, times two
pg068_n0035: b to c equals six to ten
pg068_n0036: b to c equals six to ten
pg068_n0037: Therefore, a to b to c equals three to six to ten, and a to c equals three to ten.

pg072_n0005: Proportion is essential in solving real-life problems involving scaling, ratios, and percentages.
pg072_n0006: Such problems involve comparing and relating different quantities.

pg072_n0018: The concept of equivalent fractions describes correctly what it means by a proportion.
pg072_n0019: For example, one-half and two-fourths are equivalent, and hence the two fractions are proportional.
pg072_n0020: Thus, a proportion is a statement which shows that two ratios are equal.
pg072_n0021: That means, if two ratios are proportional, the corresponding parts of each ratio have the same relationship.
pg072_n0023: Proportions can be written in two ways:
pg072_n0024: part a. As two equal fractions;
pg072_n0025: a over b equals c over d
pg072_n0027: When two ratios are equal, that is
pg072_n0028: a to b equals c to d
pg072_n0030: a over b equals c over d
pg072_n0032: a times d equals b times c
pg072_n0034: When three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then c is called the third proportional.
pg072_n0035: The third proportional of two numbers a and b is defined as
pg072_n0036: a to b equals b to c
pg072_n0038: a over b equals b over c
pg072_n0043: Find the proportional parts of one hundred fifty-six in the ratio three to four to five.

pg072_n0048: The sum of the terms of the ratio is three plus four plus five equals twelve.
pg072_n0050: three twelfths times one hundred fifty-six equals thirty-nine.
pg072_n0051: four twelfths times one hundred fifty-six equals fifty-two.
pg072_n0052: five twelfths times one hundred fifty-six equals sixty-five.
pg072_n0053: Therefore, the required proportional parts are thirty-nine, fifty-two, and sixty-five.
pg073_n0005: The first, second, third, and fourth terms are proportional.
pg073_n0006: If the first, second, and third terms are forty-two, thirty-six, and thirty-five, respectively, find the fourth term.

pg073_n0015: forty-two times x equals thirty-five times thirty-six.
pg073_n0016: x equals thirty-five times thirty-six over forty-two.
pg073_n0018: Therefore, the fourth term is thirty.

pg078_im005: Introduction to algebra: Algebra uses letters, numbers, and symbols to solve real-life problems involving unknown quantities. The chapter covers algebraic expressions, equations with one and two unknowns, and inequalities, with applications such as shopping, travel planning, recipes, profit and loss, and currency conversion.
pg078_n0009: Algebra is a branch of mathematics that helps to solve real-life problems by using letters, numbers, and symbols.
pg078_n0010: It unifies all branches of mathematics, and thus, it is a tool used in daily life activities.
pg078_n0011: Algebra is used to understand and work with unknown quantities in various situations.
pg078_n0012: For instance, it helps to calculate expenditure when shopping, plan travel routes, cooking or preparing recipes for different servings.
pg078_n0013: In this chapter, you will learn about algebraic expressions, equations with one unknown, equations with two unknowns, and inequalities with one unknown.
pg078_n0014: The competencies developed will enable you to solve daily life problems such as planning for recipes, scheduling routes, estimating profit and loss, currency conversions, among many other applications.
pg078_n0018: In algebra, letters or symbols are used to represent numbers.
pg078_n0019: For instance, it is common to represent the length of an object by the letter l, radius by letter r, and diameter by letter d.
pg078_n0020: In addition, letters such as x, y, z, α and β can be used to represent numbers.
pg078_n0022: An algebraic expression is a mathematical statement which contains numbers, letters and mathematical operations such as plus, minus, times, and divided by.
pg078_n0023: An algebraic expression is made up of terms.
pg078_n0025: A term can be a number, a variable, a number multiplied by a variable, or a variable multiplied by a variable.
pg078_n0026: For example, in the algebraic expression five x minus three y plus eight, terms are five x, minus three y and eight.
pg078_n0027: Terms with the same variables and exponents are called like terms.
pg078_n0028: For example, eight y and nine y or eight x y and three x y or six x squared y and two x squared y are like terms.
pg078_n0029: Terms with different variables or exponents are called unlike terms.
pg078_n0030: For example, six x and six z or three m n and four v y or six u squared y and two u y squared are unlike terms.
pg079_n0004: Simplification of algebraic expressions involves combining like terms by adding or subtracting their coefficients in order to obtain a simple term.
pg079_n0005: It may also involve multiplying and dividing terms as well as working with fractions and brackets.
pg079_n0007: Addition and subtraction of algebraic expressions
pg079_n0009: The basic principle of addition and subtraction of algebraic expressions is that, only like terms can be added or subtracted.

pg086_n0019: An algebraic equation is a mathematical statement connecting two algebraic expressions with an equal sign, equals.
pg086_n0020: It expresses a statement or a problem in a clear and short way.
pg086_n0021: For example, two x equals sixteen and three x plus four y equals eight are algebraic equations.
pg086_n0022: Therefore, an equation has two equal sides, the left-hand side and the right-hand side.
pg086_n0026: A linear equation is an algebraic equation in which each variable has an exponent of one.

pg121_n0009: Coordinate geometry is the branch of Mathematics which helps to uniquely determine the positions and movements of objects.
pg121_n0010: It also helps to understand the relationship between points on a plane using ordered pairs of coordinates.
pg121_n0011: In this chapter, you will learn about gradient or slope of a straight line, equation of a straight line, graphing straight lines as well as solving linear simultaneous equations graphically.
pg121_n0012: The competencies developed will enable you in solving problems such as plotting and analysing graphs, surveying and locating places, locating plot boundaries, interpreting traffic information, constructing buildings and roads and many other applications.
pg121_n0016: Coordinate geometry uses ordered pairs of numbers to describe the positions of points on the x y-coordinate plane.
pg121_n0017: The x y-coordinate plane or x y-plane is made up of two lines intersecting at right angles as shown in Figure 6.1.
pg121_im003: Chapter Six page titled 'Coordinate geometry,' with an introduction and a graph of the x y-coordinate plane showing the x- and y-axes intersecting at the origin and dividing the plane into four quadrants labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4.
pg122_n0004: Each point on a plane is uniquely represented by means of an ordered pair of real numbers called the coordinates of a point.
pg122_n0005: The x y-plane is divided into four parts called quadrants, as shown in Figure six point one.
pg122_n0006: The first quadrant, one, has positive values of x and y; the second quadrant, two, has negative values of x and positive values of y.
pg122_n0007: The third quadrant, three, has all negative values of x and y, and the fourth quadrant, four, has positive x values and negative y values.
pg122_n0008: Recall that the positions of points on the x y-plane are determined by using the x and y coordinates.
pg122_n0009: For example, for the point, open parenthesis four, six, close parenthesis, the first number, four, represents a distance from the origin along the x-axis, and six represents a distance from the origin along the y-axis.

pg007_n0012_easy_read: Mathematics is part of almost everything we do.
pg007_n0013_easy_read:
People use Mathematics in many fields, such as:
- science
- engineering
- technology
- social studies
- economics
- many others
pg007_n0014_easy_read:
Many devices use mathematical knowledge in their design and making, such as:
- mobile phones
- computers
- television sets
- satellites
pg007_n0015_easy_read:
In this chapter, you will learn about:
- the meaning of Mathematics
- the branches of Mathematics
- the relationship between Mathematics and other subjects
- the importance of studying Mathematics
pg007_n0016_easy_read:
The skills you develop will help you use Mathematics to solve daily life problems in different fields, such as:
- Agriculture
- Entrepreneurship
- Botany
- Zoology
- Music
- History
- Business
- many other fields
pg007_n0020_easy_read:
The word ‘Mathematics’ comes from the Greek word ‘mathema’.
It means ‘which is learnt’ or ‘science, knowledge or learning’.
pg007_n0021_easy_read: Numbers, measurements, shapes of physical objects, and equations are only a small part of Mathematics.
pg007_n0022_easy_read:
Mathematics can be seen as the science of:
- structures
- order
- patterns
- relations
These ideas grew from simple activities like counting, measuring, and describing the shapes of objects.
pg007_n0023_easy_read:
Mathematics can also be seen as a language of science.
By using mathematical reasoning, people can understand things better and predict nature.
pg007_n0024_easy_read: Mathematics can give a precise expression for every concept that people can write with mathematical symbols and structures.
pg007_n0025_easy_read: Mathematics knowledge and skills are very important for understanding ideas in other subjects, in both sciences and arts.
pg007_n0029_easy_read:
Mathematics has different branches, such as:
- Arithmetic
- Algebra
- Geometry
pg008_n0006_easy_read: Arithmetic is a branch of Mathematics. It deals with the properties of numbers and how people use numbers.
pg008_n0007_easy_read:
People work with numbers by using basic math operations:
- addition
- subtraction
- multiplication
- division
pg008_n0011_easy_read: Algebra is a branch of Mathematics. In algebra, people use symbols instead of specific numbers in arithmetic operations.
pg008_n0012_easy_read: The symbols or letters in algebra are called variables. Variables stand for quantities that do not have fixed values.
pg008_n0016_easy_read:
The word geometry comes from two Greek words:
- ‘Geo’, which means ‘earth’
- ‘metry’, which means ‘measurement’
pg008_n0017_easy_read: So, Geometry is a branch of Mathematics. It studies the sizes, shapes, positions, angles, and dimensions of physical objects.
pg008_n0018_easy_read:
Geometry also studies:
- points
- lines
- planes
- similarities
- congruence
- shapes of different regular objects
pg008_n0022_easy_read: Mathematics is used in every part of our lives.
pg008_n0023_easy_read: Mathematics is very important for understanding other subjects well.
pg008_n0024_easy_read: Mathematics is used to describe many concepts in other subjects and fields in a precise way.
pg008_n0025_easy_read: Learning Mathematics can help students develop problem-solving skills and critical thinking skills.
pg008_n0026_easy_read: Mathematics formulas can represent and describe concepts and situations in other fields. These formulas are commonly called mathematical models.
pg008_n0032_easy_read: Step one. Think about your daily activities. Identify and write down how Mathematics is used in those activities.

pg051_n0037_easy_read: Rounding decimals uses a similar process to rounding numbers by place value.
pg051_n0038_easy_read: When you round decimals, drop the digits to the right of the decimal place you are rounding to. Do not replace them with zeros.
pg051_n0040_easy_read: Use these steps to round off:
pg051_n0041_easy_read: (a) If the digit after the rounding digit is 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4, the rounding digit stays the same. Drop all the digits to the right.
pg051_n0050_easy_read: The digit in the 3rd decimal place is 6. The digit to the right is 4, and 4 is less than 5.
pg051_n0051_easy_read: In this case, 6 stays the same and 4 is dropped.
pg051_n0052_easy_read: So, 0.2464 is approximately equal to 0.246 to 3 decimal places.
pg052_n0003_easy_read: (b) If the digit to the right of the rounding digit is more than 5, add 1 to the rounding digit. Then remove the digits to the right.
pg052_n0010_easy_read: The digit in the third decimal place is 3. The digit to its right is 8. The digit 8 is more than 5.
pg052_n0011_easy_read: In this case, add 1 to the rounding digit. Then remove each digit to the right.
pg052_n0012_easy_read: So, 0.97381 is approximately equal to 0.974 to 3 decimal places.

pg055_n0041_easy_read: A significant figure is a digit in a number. It shows information about how exact the measured value is.
pg055_n0046_easy_read: 1. Any digit from 1 to 9 in a number is a significant figure.
pg055_n0048_easy_read: 2. A zero between digits 1 to 9 is a significant figure.
pg055_n0049_easy_read: For example, the zero in 602 is a significant figure.
pg055_n0052_easy_read: 3. Zeros to the right of the last non-zero digit are not significant figures.
pg055_n0053_easy_read: For example, 72,000 has only 2 significant figures.
pg055_n0055_easy_read: 4. In decimal numbers, any zero to the left of the first non-zero digit is not a significant figure.
pg055_n0056_easy_read: For example, the zeros in 0.025 are not significant figures.
pg055_n0059_easy_read: 5. Zeros on the right side of a decimal point are significant figures only when no non-zero digit comes after them.
pg055_n0060_easy_read: For example: dash 0.040 has 2 significant figures. dash 0.6700 has 4 significant figures. dash 10.000 has 5 significant figures.
pg056_n0007_easy_read: If zero is at the end of an approximated number, including a decimal number, zero is a significant figure.
pg056_n0008_easy_read: For example, 2.73 is approximately equal to 3.0. In this example, zero is a significant figure.
pg056_n0009_easy_read: Also, 45,961 is approximately equal to 46,000. In this number, the zero in the third place value is a significant figure.
pg056_n0013_easy_read: All zeros to the right of a non-zero digit are significant if they come from measurements.
pg056_n0014_easy_read: For example, 20 meters has 2 significant figures. 300 grams has 3 significant figures.

pg056_n0021_easy_read: Roman numeral two. Always count significant figures from left to right in a number.

pg078_n0018_easy_read: In algebra, letters or symbols can represent numbers.
pg078_n0019_easy_read:
For example, people often use:
- l for the length of an object
- r for the radius
- d for the diameter
pg078_n0020_easy_read: Also, letters such as x, y, z, alpha, and beta can represent numbers.
pg078_n0022_easy_read:
An algebraic expression is a mathematical statement.
It contains numbers, letters, and mathematical operations such as plus, minus, times, and divided by.
pg078_n0023_easy_read: An algebraic expression is made of terms.
pg078_n0025_easy_read:
A term can be:
- a number
- a variable
- a number multiplied by a variable
- a variable multiplied by a variable
pg078_n0026_easy_read:
For example, in the algebraic expression five x minus three y plus eight, the terms are:
- five x
- minus three y
- eight
pg078_n0027_easy_read: Terms with the same variables and exponents are called like terms.
pg078_n0028_easy_read:
For example, these are like terms:
- eight y and nine y
- eight x y and three x y
- six x squared y and two x squared y
pg078_n0029_easy_read: Terms with different variables or exponents are called unlike terms.
pg078_n0030_easy_read:
For example, these are unlike terms:
- six x and six z
- three m n and four v y
- six u squared y and two u y squared
pg079_n0004_easy_read:
To simplify algebraic expressions, combine like terms.
Add or subtract their coefficients to get a simpler term.
pg079_n0005_easy_read:
It can also include:
- multiplying terms
- dividing terms
- working with fractions
- working with brackets
pg079_n0009_easy_read:
The basic rule for adding and subtracting algebraic expressions is this:
You can only add or subtract like terms.

Coordinate geometry is a branch of Mathematics.
It helps you find the exact position and movement of objects.
pg121_n0010_easy_read:
Coordinate geometry also helps you understand how points on a plane are related.
It uses ordered pairs of coordinates.
pg121_n0011_easy_read:
In this chapter, you will learn about:
- gradient, or slope, of a straight line
- the equation of a straight line
- graphing straight lines
- solving linear simultaneous equations on a graph
pg121_n0012_easy_read:

- plotting and analyzing graphs
- surveying and locating places
- locating plot boundaries
- interpreting traffic information
- constructing buildings and roads
- many other applications
pg121_n0016_easy_read: Coordinate geometry uses ordered pairs of numbers to describe where points are on the x y-coordinate plane.
pg121_n0017_easy_read:
The x y-coordinate plane, or x y-plane, is made of 2 lines.
The 2 lines cross at right angles, as shown in Figure 6.1.
pg122_n0004_easy_read:
Each point on a plane has 1 ordered pair of real numbers.
This ordered pair is called the point's coordinates.
pg122_n0005_easy_read:
The x y-plane is divided into 4 parts.
These parts are called quadrants, as shown in Figure 6.1.
pg122_n0006_easy_read:
In the first quadrant, x and y are positive.
In the second quadrant, x is negative and y is positive.
pg122_n0007_easy_read:
In the third quadrant, x and y are negative.
In the fourth quadrant, x is positive and y is negative.
pg122_n0008_easy_read: Remember: You find the position of points on the x y-plane by using the x-coordinate and the y-coordinate.
pg122_n0009_easy_read:
For example, look at the point, 4 comma 6.
The first number, 4, shows the distance from the origin along the x-axis.
The number 6 shows the distance from the origin along the y-axis.

pg126_n0011_easy_read: A straight line is made by joining two different points.
pg126_n0012_easy_read: Any two points on a straight line can define the line.
pg126_n0013_easy_read: The gradient describes the type of straight line.
pg126_n0014_easy_read: This means the line can be: horizontal, vertical, or slanted.
pg126_n0015_easy_read: People use gradient in many real-life activities, such as: lifting heavy loads, climbing mountains, finding steepness in road construction, and other applications.
pg126_n0016_easy_read: Do Activity 6.2 to learn how to recognize the gradient of a straight line.
pg126_n0021_easy_read: Step 1. Use graph paper. Plot these points on the same x y plane: A, open parenthesis 2, 1, close parenthesis; B, open parenthesis 5, 6, close parenthesis; C, open parenthesis 2, 7, close parenthesis; D, open parenthesis 6, 1, close parenthesis.

pg126_n0027_easy_read: Step 4. The relationship between the ratios from step 3 is called the gradient of a line.
pg126_n0029_easy_read: Step 5. Explain how the value from task 3 shows the type of line.
pg126_n0031_easy_read: A gradient measures how steep a straight line is. It is usually written as m.
pg126_n0032_easy_read: Another name for gradient is slope.
pg126_n0033_easy_read: In coordinate geometry, the standard way to define the gradient of a straight line is to find this ratio: the change in y, vertical increase, to the change in x, horizontal increase.
pg126_n0034_easy_read: Gradient, m, equals change in y-coordinates over change in x-coordinates.
pg126_n0036_easy_read: Consider a line that passes through the points A, open parenthesis x one, y one, close parenthesis, and B, open parenthesis x two, y two, close parenthesis.
pg126_n0037_easy_read: Also, consider a right-angled triangle A B C with the straight line A B shown in Figure 6.2.
pg126_n0038_easy_read: The gradient of a line through points A and B is the ratio of the length of the vertical side of the triangle to the length of the horizontal side of
pg127_n0005_easy_read: The length of the vertical side B C of the triangle is the difference between the y-coordinates of points B and C. That is, y two minus y one, or y one minus y two.
pg127_n0006_easy_read: The length of the horizontal side of the triangle is the difference between the x-coordinates of points A and C. That is, x two minus x one, or x one minus x two.
pg127_n0008_easy_read: Figure 6.2: A straight line A B with horizontal and vertical changes
pg127_n0010_easy_read: Figure 6.2 shows the formula for the gradient m of the straight line A B:
pg127_n0011_easy_read: m equals change in y, vertical increase, over change in x, horizontal increase.
pg127_n0012_easy_read: Thus, m equals the quantity y two minus y one over x two minus x one, equals the quantity y one minus y two over x one minus x two.
pg127_n0014_easy_read: Follow these steps to calculate the gradient of a straight line that joins two points, A, open parenthesis x one, y one, close parenthesis, and B, open parenthesis x two, y two, close parenthesis.
pg127_n0017_easy_read: Step 1. Write the formula for the gradient: m equals the quantity y two minus y one over x two minus x one.
pg127_n0019_easy_read: Step 2. Put the values into open parenthesis x one, y one, close parenthesis and open parenthesis x two, y two, close parenthesis.
pg127_n0021_easy_read: Step 3. Substitute the values into the formula to get the gradient m.
pg127_n0023_easy_read: Step 4. Write the final answer, which is the gradient m.
